name: Indiana Dunes National Park
blurb: Lake Michigan dunes, oak savanna and marsh, and the animals that live between them.

tip.title: Take away fire
tip.text: Fire keeps oak savanna open. Set Fire to -100% and watch the oaks and milkweed, then the deer, monarchs and rabbits that depend on them.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Indiana Dunes National Park, Oak savanna, Ammophila (plant)). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Drives plant growth on open dunes, in wetlands and in the oak woods.
Wikipedia says fire, lit by people or lightning, kept oak savannas from turning into closed forest by favouring fire-tolerant oaks.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the sand and soil.
A pine of sandy ground, recorded often near the park and listed in GloBI as food for deer, red squirrels and white-footed mice.
A prairie wildflower and the food plant of monarch caterpillars. GloBI also records rabbits eating it.
Marsh plants that fill the wet hollows between dune ridges and feed muskrats.
One of the common large animals of the park. Browses woody plants and wildflowers and supplies food for coyotes, bobcats and vultures.
Eats grasses and wildflowers such as milkweed, and is prey for foxes, coyotes, raccoons and bobcats.
The most-recorded mammal in the GBIF data. Eats seeds of pines and other trees and is eaten by coyotes and foxes.
A small seed-eating rodent of woods and dune scrub that feeds snakes, foxes and coyotes.
A marsh rodent that feeds on cattails and other water plants and is taken by herons, foxes, raccoons and coyotes.
Caterpillars feed only on milkweed, and adults sip nectar from flowers such as milkweed, buttonbush and beebalm.
Wading bird of marshes and shores. GloBI records it eating frogs, snakes, voles and muskrats.
A common omnivore that GloBI records eating rabbits, muskrats, birds, frogs and snakes.
A common canid of the park that GloBI records preying on rabbits, squirrels, mice, muskrats and snakes.
A scavenger that cleans up dead deer, rabbits and muskrats, as GloBI records.
Top mammal predator here. GloBI records it eating rabbits, squirrels, mice, muskrats, beavers and deer.
Wikipedia says bobcats were photographed in the park again around 2018. A cat that hunts rabbits, rodents and young deer.

story: Indiana Dunes National Park runs about 15 miles along the southern shore of Lake Michigan and covers 15,349 acres. Congress authorized it in 1966 as a national lakeshore, and it became the nation's 61st national park in 2019.
matters: Beachgrasses grow on the first line of coastal dunes, and their creeping underground stems hold shifting sand. The park also includes outlying areas such as Pinhook Bog and Hoosier Prairie.
